scenario.prompt_to_agent:
PC1 (10.1.0.100) in Office A on VLAN 10 reports its default
gateway (10.1.0.1) is intermittently unreachable but eventually
responds. Latency to the gateway is higher than normal. Other
hosts on VLAN 10 report the same. VLAN 40 (Laptop1) and VLAN 99
hosts are unaffected. Investigate.

pre_check.command: ip -br link show br0.10 | grep -c UP

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show br0.10 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dswa1 br10 SVI (10.1.0.2/24)
Mechanism: dswa1 is the VRRP MASTER for the VLAN 10 VIP
  10.1.0.1 (priority 105). When its br10 SVI goes down,
  keepalived on dswa1 stops sending VRRP advertisements,
  and dswa2 (BACKUP, priority 1) eventually takes over
  the VIP. The handoff causes the intermittent reachability
  pattern users observe. Once dswa2 is MASTER, PC1 reaches
  the gateway again, but at higher cost (extra L2 hop).
Localization: dswa1
Root cause: br10 bridge interface administratively down on dswa1
Fix: `ip link set br10 up` on dswa1
scenario.fix_spec: `ip link set br10 up` on dswa1

line.command: ip -br link show br0.10 | grep -c UP

agent.diagnosis_text:
The VLAN 10 SVI (`br0.10`) on dswa1 is administratively shut down. The interface has the IP address 10.1.0.2/24 configured but carries neither the `UP` flag nor the `LOWER_UP` flag — it is operator-downed and in kernel state `DOWN`. This is the only VLAN sub-interface on dswa1 that is not up; `br0.20`, `br0.40`, and `br0.99` are all fully operational, which is exactly why VLAN 40 and VLAN 99 hosts are unaffected.

The fault produces the reported symptom through the following mechanism. dswa1 is the STP root bridge (bridge-ID `1000.166cd8e0368c`). As a result, aswa2's uplink toward dswa2 (`eth2`) is in STP blocking state, so all frames from PC1 (and every other VLAN 10 host behind aswa2) must pass through dswa1. Because dswa1's `br0.10` is down, dswa1 cannot itself answer as the Layer-3 gateway for 10.1.0.1. The VLAN 10 gateway VIP (`10.1.0.1/32`) lives exclusively on dswa2's `br0.10` (which is UP). For PC1's ARP or ICMP to reach 10.1.0.1 it must travel `PC1 → aswa2 → dswa1 → peer-link bond0 → dswa2` — confirmed by dswa2's MAC/ARP table showing PC1's MAC arriving on `bond0` (the inter-distribution peer link) rather than on dswa2's own downlink. The return path is symmetrically suboptimal. This extra peer-link hop raises round-trip latency and causes intermittent drops each time ARP or MAC table entries age out and must be re-resolved across the longer path.

Root cause: `br0.10` was brought administratively down on dswa1, silently stranding all Office-A VLAN 10 traffic on a peer-link detour to dswa2.

Corrective fix: On dswa1, run `ip link set br0.10 up`. Verify with `ip link show br0.10` (should show `<BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP>`) and confirm PC1 can ping 10.1.0.1 with normal sub-millisecond latency. Persist the fix in dswa1's startup configuration so the interface is raised at every container start.

per_axis.rationale: The agent repeatedly and explicitly identifies dswa1 as the affected device (e.g., 'on dswa1' and describing its interfaces and state).
The agent explicitly identifies the VLAN 10 SVI on dswa1 (named br0.10) as administratively down, matching the required component (VLAN 10 SVI / br10).

The writeup fails to describe VRRP/keepalived behavior or the MASTER→BACKUP takeover on dswa1 failure and incorrectly states the VIP lives on dswa2 instead of explaining that dswa2 becomes MASTER when dswa1's SVI goes down.
Recommends bringing br0.10 up on dswa1 and persisting it, which matches the expected fix to restore the VLAN 10 SVI.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations (dswa1 br0.10 state DOWN; dswa2 br0.10 UP; STP root IDs; aswa2 STP blocking) and FDB/ARP evidence supporting the detour via the peer link, so the conclusion that an admin-down SVI on dswa1 caused the suboptimal path is well supported. Minor missing explicit VRRP state output or an explicit print showing the VIP on dswa2 is inferred from observed addresses, but the inference is logical and covered by the collected evidence.
